subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should session maintenance delete old `.bak.*` transcript rotation archives and run proactive startup or timer sweeps by default, or should those remain explicit cleanup/disk-budget behavior?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves `.bak.*` in normal retention tests and docs explicitly avoid startup pruning, so changing this behavior requires lifecycle and data-retention intent rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Land the narrow deleted/reset fix first
options.body: Keep the current no-startup-prune and `.bak.*` retention semantics while improving operator visibility for deleted/reset cleanup through the existing open PR or equivalent.

options.title: Add explicit `.bak.*` retention policy
options.body: Define a tested retention rule for `.bak.*` archives before deleting them outside disk-budget pressure.

options.title: Add proactive default sweeps
options.body: Run cleanup at gateway startup or on a timer, accepting the compatibility and performance risk of automatic filesystem mutation.

recommendation.title: Land the narrow deleted/reset fix first
recommendation.body: Keep the current no-startup-prune and `.bak.*` retention semantics while improving operator visibility for deleted/reset cleanup through the existing open PR or equivalent.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the cleanup CLI and disk-budget behavior that the remaining policy would extend or preserve.
